prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system, through PROTACs and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the one shortlisted candidate that four colleagues placed first, and having ranked it third myself I am persuaded it deserves to lead. It is a new chemical modality with clear mechanism: a designed small molecule brings an E3 ligase and a target together, and the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery does the rest. The concept (Crews and Deshaies, with Sakamoto) is original, and the cereblon discovery (Handa) explains how thalidomide-class molecular glues work at the molecular level. Independent laboratories have confirmed the mechanism in depth, including ternary-complex structure and cooperativity, and the field now has a large clinical pipeline. A three-person prize joining the PROTAC concept with the cereblon mechanism gives a coherent citation covering both strands.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader has yet reached approval, so the therapeutic payoff that would make the prize clearly timely is still unproven, and this is the main reason I did not rank it first. Attribution is also hard: Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim all made decisive contributions, and any three-name set leaves out people the field regards as central. Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one discovery or two is a genuine question for the citation.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B023 first but proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned the PROTAC concept into a general, drug-like platform.
responses.response: I accept that Ciulli's structural and mechanistic work is what made PROTACs general, and I could be persuaded either way. I still prefer Handa as the third name. Without the cereblon mechanism the molecular-glue strand, which is where the clinical compounds are furthest along, is absent from the citation. Ciulli's contribution is a platform-engineering step on an existing concept, whereas Handa's is a discovery of mechanism. I would want the committee to decide this explicitly rather than by default.

responses.point: Aili ranks B023 first as a conceptually clean idea of hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system, with Handa underpinning the molecular-glue half, and notes that timing is somewhat early with no approved PROTAC.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution and with the timing caveat. I would add that early timing matters less here than for other candidates, because the mechanism is confirmed independently in many groups; what is pending is clinical outcome, not understanding. That distinguishes B023 from B021, which Aili ranks second, where the disagreement is about what is physically happening in cells.

responses.point: Zou ranks Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (B002) first as a mature, industrially proven, ligand-controlled method, ranking B023 fourth as possibly premature.
responses.response: I respect the maturity of B002 and agree that its science is beyond dispute. My reservation is that the 2010 prize on Pd cross-coupling, which a committee could read as already covering the field, weakens the novelty. Buchwald-Hartwig also overlaps in credit with Kosugi, a point on which I do not feel the case is fully settled. I would not oppose B002, but I do not think the premature-timing objection to B023 outweighs these points.

responses.point: Sparr ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B041) first as a physical-chemistry achievement that enabled siRNA and mRNA medicines, noting the 2023 Medicine prize left out the delivery vehicle.
responses.response: The lipid chemistry is real and the impact is global, but I am not convinced the 2023 omission is a reason for a Chemistry prize. The attribution among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is much more diffuse than for B023, and the Medicine prize overlap makes this a more awkward choice. I regard B041 as a serious candidate for a later year rather than the strongest this year.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B002 first as fully mature and arguably overdue, and ranks B023 last on the shortlist as possibly early.
responses.response: I take the maturity argument seriously, and it is where B023 is weakest. I disagree on what it implies: the chemistry of degraders is settled at the mechanistic level even though approval is pending, and the Nobel tradition has often honoured concepts before their full application. I would ask whether the committee prefers recognition that is late and safe or timely and conceptually new.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli or Handa belongs in the third place with Crews and Deshaies, and whether the prize treats PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes the prize premature.
Whether B028 (proton-coupled electron transfer) should be preferred; my own research interest is close, so I cannot judge its place without bias.
statement.conflict_note: I work on proton transfer and biological energy conversion, close to B028 (PCET), so I discount my own first-place opening ranking of that candidate. I am a Stockholm University colleague of committee member Xiaodong Zou, who is not a candidate. No specific conflict with B023 is apparent from the provided profile.
